hex_grid <- function(x, cell_size, clip = TRUE) {
  stopifnot(is.numeric(cell_size), length(cell_size) == 1, cell_size > 0)
  stopifnot(is_sf(x) || is_sfc(x))
  x <- as_sf(x)
  if (!all(c("x", "y") %in% names(x))) stop("x must contain x and y columns")
  # Flat-topped hexagons have a horizontal axis of length cell_size.
  # The vertical axis is cell_size * sqrt(3) / 2.
  dx <- cell_size
  dy <- cell_size * sqrt(3) / 2
  # Offset the grid so the first cell sits at the lower-left corner of the
  # bounding box.
  x_min <- min(x$x, na.rm = TRUE)
  x_max <- max(x$x, na.rm = TRUE)
  y_min <- min(x$y, na.rm = TRUE)
  y_max <- max(x$y, na.rm = TRUE)
  col <- floor((x$x - x_min) / dx)
  row <- floor((y_min - x$y) / dy)
  # Cells outside the bounding box are dropped unless clip = TRUE.
  if (clip) {
    keep <- abs(col - (x_max - x_min) / dx) <= 1 / dx &&
      abs(row - (y_max - y_min) / dy) <= 1 / dy
    col <- col[keep]
    row <- row[keep]
  }
  # Each cell is a hexagon with three vertices per side.
  half <- dx / 2
  vert <- cbind(
    x = x_min + col * dx + half * c(-1, 0, 1),
    y = y_min + row * dy + half * c(-1, 1, 1)
  )
  # Return one row per hexagon.
  out <- unique(vert)
  out$cell_id <- paste0("h", row, "_", col)
  out
}
